relevance_note: The paper describes four of its own patients with homozygous GAMT variants and 44 literature cases individually: 'The proband is an 8-year-old boy with a homozygous missense pathogenic variant in the GAMT gene'.
method_note: Read the paper in full and built the JSON with a Python script in the scratch directory; Table 1 and Table 2 rows were parsed from the Markdown and every feature bullet was asserted to occur in its cell; spans are row segments from the case-number cell through the cited cell. Scope: 4 first-hand cases (Case 1-4, also Table 1; the paper says they were previously described in ref 9), 44 literature cases in Table 2 (Case No. 5-48; labelled 'Table 2 #n' because the Case No. column holds bare numbers, except #38 which the text calls 'case 38'), and 2 previously published individuals described in the Discussion with individual-level facts ('ref ^48 patient', diagnosed at 8 days; 'ref ^51 patient', diagnosed prenatally). The ref ^48 patient (Viau et al.) may be the same person as Table 2 #20 (Viau et al 2013, normal development) but the paper does not say so; not merged. Literature cases: no sex, age or variant is given per patient; each gets a variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported', tied by the named-group statement '44 literature cases of patients with confirmed pathogenic variants in the GAMT gene' (also used for pathogenicity and diagnosis basis). Features come only from the Clinical outcome, EEG and MRI/MRS columns; 'NM' cells are not reported. 'Seizure-free' outcomes alone (#14, #15, #40, #44) were not taken as evidence of seizures; 'Controlled seizure', 'No improvement for seizures' and 'Short seizure' were. Outcomes such as 'Improve motor function', 'less concern for autistic behavior' (#18), 'Slow progress in development' (#23) and 'Multiple tiermolds' (#45, unintelligible) were not recorded as features. MRS findings (reduced creatine peak) are recorded as features but not mapped to the MRI lesion checklist items. 'Normal MRI' / MRI normal is recorded as 'abnormal brain MRI' excluded (a whole investigation; per D-27 it does not exclude the more specific MRI checklist items, which stay not reported). 'Normal EEG'/'Normal' in the EEG column excludes the 'abnormal eeg' item (#19, #37). 'Normal development' (#20, ref ^48, ref ^51) was taken to exclude the developmental delay or intellectual disability item. Case 1 'normal power, tone, and reflexes' excludes hypotonia and (as normal tone) spasticity. 'Speech delay' alone was not mapped to 'absent or limited speech'; Case 2 'restriction in language development', #31 'No expressive language' and #40 'has not shown any active speech development' were. Cognitive impairment (#31) was not mapped to the DD/ID item. Contradictions: case 38 has 'Generalized hypertonia and rigidity' in Table 2 but 'hypotonia and rigidity progressed' in the text (both rows emitted; hypotonia checklist not reported). Case 1 and Case 2 carry the same c.160G > C described on different transcripts (NM_138924.2 vs NM_000156.6). Case 3 variant printed as 'exon6:x.577c > T:pQ193X' (recorded verbatim in cdna/protein fields, with 'x.' rather than 'c.'). Case 3 is a girl but the text says 'his seizure pattern'. Case 2 creatinine maximum '450 mg' in text vs '350–450 mg/kg/day' in Table 1. Abstract says 52 cases and male-to-female 3:1; Results say 48 patients, 27 male and 21 female. Table 2 #42 cites Mudd et al 2001 (ref 30), whose title in the reference list is glycine N-methyltransferase deficiency, yet the paper counts it among GAMT cases. Ref 48 in the reference list (Viau-Guay, person-centered care) does not match the Viau et al. study cited in the Discussion. Ethnicity 'Saudi Arabia' for Cases 1-4 is from the abstract's named-group statement '4 novel cases from Saudi Arabia'. Case 4 onset left not reported (the paper gives age at presentation, 4 years, not onset). Lennox-Gastaut in Case 1 ('suggestive of') not recorded as hedged; recorded for Case 2 ('labeled as'). Case 4 variant type 'missense' from 'predicted to result in an amino acid substitution'.
